demand.title: Heating demand
demand.description: Optional: per thermostat an entity that says how much it heats – a percentage (e.g. the heating power of a cloud integration) or an on/off value (e.g. a threshold helper on a pipe sensor). Tado X reports neither its valve nor its demand over Matter, so thermostats without one show no heating status.

error.thermostat_in_other_room: A thermostat already belongs to another room.
error.demand_not_numeric: This sensor does not report a number.
error.room_thermostat: A room thermostat of this integration cannot be a room's thermostat.

thermostat_unconfirmed.title: {thermostat} does not take its setting
thermostat_unconfirmed.description:
The room {room} sent {thermostat} a new setting more than 30 minutes ago, and the thermostat has not reported it back. It is probably hard to reach in the Thread network, or its batteries are low.

The integration sends the setting again when the thermostat reconnects or reports; this message goes away once it confirms.

window_chatter.title: A window contact of {room} keeps bouncing
window_chatter.description:
{count} openings in {room} in the last hour were shorter than the room's open delay. The room ignores them, but a contact that bounces usually has a loose magnet or a door that does not close properly.

Check the contact, or raise the room's "Switch off after" if people often open the door briefly. This message goes away after an hour without bouncing.

window_contact_unavailable.title: Window contact {contact} is gone while open
window_contact_unavailable.description:
{contact} in {room} has been unavailable for 30 minutes, and the last it said was open – so {room} stays switched off until it reports again.

Check its battery and connection. If the window is closed, the room heats again as soon as the contact reports.

tado_overwriting.title: Something overwrites setpoints in several rooms
tado_overwriting.description:
Thermostats in {rooms} were changed outside Tado X Matter Pro within a minute. People rarely do that at once; usually it is the tado° app's own schedule, its "manual control" setting or its open window detection.

In the tado° app: make the schedule flat, set manual changes to last until you cancel them, and switch off open window detection – see the installation guide. This message goes away with the next restart.

resume_schedule.name: Resume schedule
resume_schedule.description: Back to the schedule: ends manual holds, timed overrides, boost and a room switched off, and skips the wait after a window closed. An open window still keeps the room off. Returns at once; the thermostats are written in the background.

boost.name: Boost
boost.description: Heats a room hard for a while, then the room returns to what applied before. Ends early on resume or a change by hand.

set_override.name: Set override
set_override.description: Heats a room at a temperature – or its comfort or eco temperature – until a time, for a while, or until the next schedule change.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Give either a temperature or a preset.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: Comfort or eco: the room's own temperature for it, as it is now.

until.name: Until
until.description: A time; if it has passed today, tomorrow.

until_next_change.name: Until the next change
until_next_change.description: The default: until the schedule changes next.

extend_block.name: Extend block
extend_block.description: Keeps the room's current plan temperature until a time, whatever the schedule says – e.g. comfort longer in the evening.

until.name: Until
until.description: A time; if it has passed today, tomorrow.

temperature_or_preset.message: Give either a temperature or a preset.
